definitions.explanation: The fourth finger, between the middle finger and the little finger. Called 薬指 ('medicine finger') because it was traditionally used to apply powdered medicine.

examples.japanese: {薬指|くすりゆび}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{指輪|ゆびわ}→指輪：01744_yubiwa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: She's wearing a ring on her ring finger.

examples.japanese: ⟦{左手|ひだりて}→左手：10975_hidarite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{薬指|くすりゆび}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{結婚指輪|けっこんゆびわ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧はめた。
examples.english: I put a wedding ring on my left ring finger.

examples.japanese: ⟦ギター→ギター：04461_gitaa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{弾|ひ}く→弾く：02444_hiku⟧とき、{薬指|くすりゆび}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{動|うご}かなくて→動く：00904_ugoku⟧⟦{苦労|くろう}した→苦労する：25357_kurousuru⟧。
examples.english: When playing guitar, I struggled because my ring finger wouldn't move the way I wanted.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The name {薬指|くすりゆび} literally means 'medicine finger.' In traditional Japanese and Chinese medicine, this finger was used to apply and mix powdered medicines because it was believed to have a gentle touch.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {薬指|くすりゆび}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{指輪|ゆびわ}→指輪：01744_yubiwa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧はめる (to put a ring on one's ring finger)
- ⟦{左手|ひだりて}→左手：10975_hidarite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{薬指|くすりゆび} (left ring finger — where wedding rings are worn)
- ⟦{右手|みぎて}→右手：10438_migite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{薬指|くすりゆび} (right ring finger)

RELATED WORDS:
The five fingers in order: ⟦{親指|おやゆび}→親指：04114_oyayubi⟧ (thumb), ⟦{人|ひと}{差|さ}し{指|ゆび}→人差し指：11471_hitosashiyubi⟧ (index finger), ⟦{中指|なかゆび}→中指：04281_nakayubi⟧ (middle finger), {薬指|くすりゆび} (ring finger), ⟦{小指|こゆび}→小指：04029_koyubi⟧ (little finger/pinky).
